original_question: Compute the unresolved essential dimensions ed_F(GL_8 / mu_2) in characteristic 2, ed_F(GL_16 / mu_2) in characteristic not 2, and ed_F(GL_{p^2} / mu_p) for odd primes p over arbitrary fields F.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it names exactly the three cases in Problem 6.5, keeps the characteristic restrictions on the first two cases, and uses the same algebraic-group formulation ed_F(GL_n/μ_m) that the paper uses immediately before stating the problem.
missing_details: State explicitly that ed_F denotes essential dimension over the base field F in the sense of Definition 6.1, i.e. for the functor H^1(-,G).
Note that the paper presents these three computations specifically as the 'smallest open cases' in Section 6, rather than as a broader neighboring problem.
Make explicit that the third clause has no characteristic hypothesis: for every odd prime p, one asks for ed_F(GL_{p^2}/μ_p) over arbitrary base fields F.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, include the nearby identification H^1(-,GL_n/μ_m) with isomorphism classes of central simple algebras of degree n and period dividing m.
Avoid adding editorial wording such as 'unresolved' unless tied to the paper’s own phrasing 'smallest open cases'.
refined_question: Let F be a field, and let ed_F(G) denote the essential dimension over F of the algebraic group G, i.e. of the functor H^1(-,G). Compute ed_F(GL_8/μ_2) when char(F)=2, compute ed_F(GL_16/μ_2) when char(F)≠2, and, for every odd prime p, compute ed_F(GL_{p^2}/μ_p) over arbitrary fields F.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the identification H^1(K,GL_n/μ_m) with the set of isomorphism classes of central simple K-algebras of degree n and period dividing m, determine the essential dimension of these algebra functors in the three cases (n,m)=(8,2) with char(F)=2, (16,2) with char(F)≠2, and (p^2,p) for odd primes p over arbitrary base fields F.
justification: This is an exact match to the paper’s official formulation. After defining essential dimension in Section 6 and identifying H^1(-,GL_n/μ_m) with central simple algebras of degree n and period dividing m, the paper states in Problem 6.5: compute ed_F(GL_8/μ_2) when char F=2; ed_F(GL_16/μ_2) when char F≠2; and ed_F(GL_{p^2}/μ_p) for odd primes p and all F. The paper also remarks that the last clause overlaps with Problem 2.1 on division algebras of prime period and crossed products.
